mocks.title: Fundamentals: two short problems

problems.label: A
problems.title: Merge two sorted linked lists
problems.prompt: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list, reusing the nodes; on equal values the first list's node comes first.
hints: What do you do with the leftover tail of one list?
A dummy head removes the special case for the first node.

problems.label: B
problems.title: Longest substring without repeats
problems.prompt: Return the length of the longest substring with no repeated character.
hints: When a character repeats, where must the window's left edge jump to?
Store each character's last index; left = max(left, last[c] + 1).

strong: dummy head, stable on ties, O(n + m) time, O(1) extra space
window with a last-seen index per character; O(n) time
traces "abba" and the empty string before saying done
followups: return the substring, not its length

mocks.title: Heaps and graphs

problems.label: A
problems.title: Top-k frequent words with a tie-break
problems.prompt: Return the k most frequent words, most frequent first; equal counts in alphabetical order.
hints: Which word should a size-k min-heap pop first when counts tie?
Sorting by (-count, word) is a correct baseline; start there.

problems.label: B
problems.title: Course schedule (topological order)
problems.prompt: Given n courses and (course, prerequisite) pairs, return an order that takes every course, or [] if none exists.
hints: Which courses can you take on day one?
Count in-degrees; repeatedly take a course with in-degree zero.

strong: compares sort O(n log n) with a size-k heap O(n log k) before coding
gets the alphabetical tie-break right inside a min-heap
Kahn's algorithm; a cycle shows up as an order shorter than n; O(V + E)
followups: return one cycle when there is no order
fewest semesters if any number of courses fit in one

mocks.title: Design-style: cache, then rate limiter

problems.label: A
problems.title: LRU cache
problems.prompt: Design a fixed-capacity cache with get and put, both O(1); when full, evict the least recently used key.
hints: Which operation forces you beyond a plain dict?
What lets you move an entry to the most-recent end in O(1)?

problems.label: B
problems.title: Rate limiter with an injectable clock
problems.prompt: Add a per-client rate limiter: allow(client) returns False once a client exceeds N requests per window.
hints: How will you test this without sleeping?
Pass a clock function into the limiter instead of calling time directly.

strong: writes the API and its O(1) targets before any data structure (see §29.1)
dict + doubly linked list, or OrderedDict with the trade-off stated
injects the clock so the limiter is testable without sleeping
followups: sliding log vs token bucket: memory per client

mocks.title: Dynamic programming

problems.label: A
problems.title: Word break (yes/no, then one split)
problems.prompt: Can string s be split into dictionary words (reuse allowed)? Then return one such split.
hints: Can you answer for every prefix of s?
ok[i] is true when some word ends at i and ok[i - len(word)] is true.

problems.label: B
problems.title: Coin change: fewest coins and number of ways
problems.prompt: Given coin values and an amount, return the fewest coins that make it (or -1), then the number of ways.
hints: What is the answer for amount 0?
For number of ways, put the coin loop outside the amount loop.

strong: states the DP recipe aloud: state, transition, base case (see §19.3)
memoised recursion first, then bottom-up; bounds the inner loop by the longest word
explains why the loop order separates combinations from orderings
followups: return all splits (the output can be exponential)

mocks.role: Data scientist or analytics engineer, technical round
mocks.title: Analytics: SQL window functions and a cohort table
segments: A: top-N per group in SQL

problems.label: A
problems.title: Top-N per region, ranks, running totals
problems.prompt: From sales(region, day, amount) in SQLite, return the n largest sales per region, then a running total per region.
hints: What should happen when two sales tie for the n-th place?
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY amount DESC).

problems.label: B
problems.title: Monthly cohort retention matrix
problems.prompt: From users and orders tables, build a cohort-by-month-offset table of the share of users with a paid order.
hints: What exactly makes a user active in a month?
Turn each month into year * 12 + month so offsets are subtraction.

strong: asks how ties rank, then picks ROW_NUMBER, RANK or DENSE_RANK on purpose
defines active (paid orders only) and the month offset before coding
checks the matrix on a three-user example worked by hand
followups: the same retention table in SQL

mocks.role: ML engineer or data scientist, ML fundamentals round
mocks.title: Metrics and leakage-free evaluation

problems.label: A
problems.title: ROC-AUC with ties
problems.prompt: Compute ROC-AUC from labels and scores without a library, handling tied scores.
hints: What does AUC mean as a probability over pairs?
Sort by score; how many negatives sit below each positive?

problems.label: B
problems.title: Cross-validation splits without leakage
problems.prompt: Write k-fold and group k-fold splitters and show how selecting features before splitting leaks.
hints: Which statistics does your preprocessing learn from the data?
Rows from one user must not sit on both sides of a split.

strong: defines AUC as P(positive scores above negative), ties counted half
moves from O(P·N) pairs to an O(n log n) rank formula with a cross-check
selects features inside each training fold; names group and time leakage
followups: a model whose AUC is high but is badly calibrated

mocks.role: ML engineer, modelling and debugging round
mocks.title: Logistic regression, then a broken training loop

problems.label: A
problems.title: Binary logistic regression with a gradient check
problems.prompt: Implement binary logistic regression with gradient descent and check your gradient numerically.
hints: What happens to exp(-z) when z is -1000?
Compare the analytic gradient with (f(w + h) - f(w - h)) / 2h.

problems.label: B
problems.title: Debug this broken training loop
problems.prompt: This training loop's accuracy is poor. Find the bug, explain the symptom and fix it.
hints: Is the loss flat, stuck at a floor, or noisy at evaluation?
Compare a first-layer weight before and after one optimiser step.

strong: overflow-safe sigmoid and a finite-difference gradient check (see §35.2)
vectorised loss and gradient; states the cost per epoch as O(n·d)
debugs by symptom, then one probe per hypothesis, then a one-line fix
followups: the loss becomes NaN at step 40: what do you check?

mocks.role: LLM or ML engineer, model internals round
mocks.title: Attention, masks and the KV cache

problems.label: A
problems.title: Scaled dot-product attention with masks
problems.prompt: Implement scaled dot-product attention with an optional boolean mask; never return NaN.
hints: What shape is Q K^T?
What does softmax return for a row of all -inf?

problems.label: B
problems.title: Causal and padding masks
problems.prompt: Build causal and padding masks by broadcasting and combine them.
hints: Which keys may query i see in a causal model?
Combine as causal & key-is-real, shape (B, 1, T, T), so it broadcasts over heads.

problems.label: C
problems.title: KV cache that matches full recompute
problems.prompt: Add a KV cache to a small decoder so incremental decoding matches full recompute.
hints: Which tensors of past tokens never change?
Each new token needs only its own query.

strong: says every tensor shape aloud and why scores are divided by sqrt(d_k)
handles a fully masked row without NaN, using a stable softmax
tests the cache against full recompute instead of trusting it
followups: KV-cache memory for a given model and context (see §39.7)
attention cost in n and d

mocks.title: BM25, hybrid fusion and an evaluation gate
segments: A: BM25 with an inverted index

problems.label: A
problems.title: BM25 from scratch
problems.prompt: Implement BM25 search over a small corpus with an inverted index.
hints: Which documents can score above zero for this query?
Keep term -> {doc: tf} postings and touch only query terms.

problems.label: B
problems.title: Hybrid retrieval with RRF
problems.prompt: Fuse a BM25 ranking and a dense ranking with reciprocal rank fusion.
hints: Why is it useful that RRF needs only ranks?
Score each doc as the sum of 1 / (k + rank) over lists.

problems.label: C
problems.title: Retrieval evaluation harness
problems.prompt: Report Recall@K and MRR over a labelled query set and fail the run if they regress.
hints: Write the expected Recall@3 for one query by hand first.
MRR uses the rank of the first relevant document only.

strong: states which IDF variant it uses and why it stays positive
scores only the postings of query terms; ties broken by doc id
measures Recall@K and MRR on labelled queries before tuning k1, b or the RRF k
followups: where a reranker goes and what it costs (see §40.6)

mocks.role: LLM application engineer, AI-assisted build round
mocks.title: Tool-calling agent loop with an assistant allowed

problems.label: A
problems.title: The function-calling loop
problems.prompt: With an assistant allowed, build the loop that calls a model, runs requested tools and returns its final answer.
hints: What stops the loop if the model never gives a final answer?
Keep the transcript as the only state.

problems.label: B
problems.title: Tool error handling and retries
problems.prompt: Make tool failures safe: retry what a retry can fix and report the rest to the model.
hints: Which failures can a retry fix, and which can only the model fix?
Inject sleep so the retry test runs instantly.

strong: plans the loop and its stop conditions before the first prompt (see §46.2)
writes tests with the mock model before reading generated code
retries only transient errors, keeps internal error text away from the model, explains every kept line
followups: validate a structured output against a schema (see §41.4)
add a fallback model behind a gateway (see §43.3)
how would you evaluate this agent offline?
